I will still do it the way I know and the way people around me do it. I have only 6 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but I will not save too hard on fertilizer and then lose yield. On my land, garlic eats fertilizer heavily, so I will feed garlic first and not let it go hungry. After garlic, I will put maize on that same ground, because that is the way we have done this rotation and I know how it behaves with my well water. Wheat is steadier and less risky, so I will keep some land in wheat for grain and cash flow. I usually start from last year’s way, then adjust a little by how prices look and how the stand came up. If neighbors use an improved seed and I see the ears or bulbs are better, I will follow that, but I will not gamble on anything too strange. Since I have well irrigation, I will use water at the key times and push the crop a bit rather than let it suffer dry stress. For 6 mu total, I will do 3 mu garlic and then summer maize on those same 3 mu, and 3 mu wheat on the other 3 mu.
